summary: Angeles NF lookout built 1934 to plan BC-301; cab burned in a 1987 fire, steel tower still stands; restoration abandoned; sources disagree on the fire's name.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 wood cab on a 20-foot H-brace open steel tower
facts.status_note: Steel tower remains; the cab burned in 1987. One trail report lists the status as demolished, which conflicts with the registry.

access.note: Reached on foot by a fire road, 6.5 miles one way from Lake Hughes Road (trail report). A Do Not Climb sign is posted on the tower. No official access rule found.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Angeles National Forest

visit.trail_note: No summit trail remains; the approach is a 6.5-mile fire road from Lake Hughes Road. A Do Not Climb sign is posted on the tower.

events.note: Constructed in 1934 to California Region 5 plan BC-301 (registry)
Newspaper (Aug 19, 1969, quoted by Forest Lookouts) says the tower first spotted smoke near a Los Angeles water reservoir; it does not name the observer
Overrun by a 1987 fire and burned; cab lost. Registry says 'Ruby Fire'; ANFFLA and Angeles Adventures say 'Ruby Ridge Fire'; Forest Lookouts describes a September 1987 fire northeast of Castaic Lake
Registered November 3, 2019; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: Registry and Angeles Adventures both give a 20-foot tower (6.1 m). The brief's 7.6 m equals 25 feet, which neither source gives.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Registry says Ruby Fire; ANFFLA and Angeles Adventures say Ruby Ridge Fire; Forest Lookouts describes a September 1987 fire near Castaic Lake. All describe the loss of the cab in 1987; the name is left as sources give it.
Angeles Adventures header says Status: Demolished, but its own text and the registry say the steel tower remains. Recorded as standing, cab gone.

notes_for_editor: 1934 build date rests on the registry alone; no newspaper or Forest Service record was read. The 1969 smoke report is quoted second-hand on a hobby page. Access is inferred from one trail report (6.5-mile fire road); no official rule found. Height corrected to 20 ft per registry and trail report. Status 'Demolished' on Angeles Adventures conflicts with the rest; kept as standing (cab gone). The brief's 'unknown' access replaced with 'public' on the basis of the trail report and no closure found. Staffing 'not staffed' as of 1987 comes from the registry's wording.
